arxiv-2510-08413.title: Prompts Generalize with Low Data: Non-vacuous Generalization Bounds for Optimizing Prompts with More Informative Priors
arxiv-2510-08413.creator: David Madras, Joshua Safyan, Qiuyi (Richard) Zhang
arxiv-2510-08413.description: Abstract Many prompt engineering techniques have been successful in practice, even when optimizing over a large prompt space with with a small amount of task-specific data. Recent work ( Akinwande et al. 2023 ) has partially explained this success by showing generalization bounds which apply PAC-Bayes theory to the discrete prompt space, but they are non-vacuous only in data-rich scenarios.

pmc-10552763.title: Bioinformatic and functional characterization of cyclic-di-GMP metabolic proteins in Vibrio alginolyticus unveils key diguanylate cyclases controlling multiple biofilm-associated phenotypes
pmc-10552763.creator: Xiao-Xiao Gong, Yan-Hua Zeng, Hai-Min Chen, Na Zhang, Yue Han, Hao Long, Zhen-Yu Xie
pmc-10552763.description: The biofilm lifestyle is critical for bacterial survival and proliferation in the fluctuating marine environment. Cyclic diguanylate (c-di-GMP) is a key second messenger during bacterial adaptation to various environmental signals, which has been identified as a master regulator of biofilm formation.

pmc-11393895.title: Modeling Realistic Geometries in Human Intrathoracic Airways
pmc-11393895.creator: Francesca Pennati, Lorenzo Aliboni, Andrea Aliverti
pmc-11393895.description: Geometrical models of the airways offer a comprehensive perspective on the complex interplay between lung structure and function. Originating from mathematical frameworks, these models have evolved to include detailed lung imagery, a crucial enhancement that aids in the early detection of morphological changes in the airways, which are often the first indicators of diseases.

pmc-11455441.creator: S Bhandari, R Elhag, J Singh, N Rastogi
pmc-11455441.description: Disclosure: S. Bhandari: None. R. Elhag: None. J. Singh: None. N. Rastogi: None. Background: Pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (NET) are rare lesions that are typically sporadic, solitary and usually <2cm in diameter, with reported incidence of 4 cases per 1 million patients per year[1]. The most common hormone secreting NET are insulinomas.

pmc-11656424.title: Variations in Furin SNPs, a Major Concern of SARS-CoV-2 Susceptibility Among Different Populations: An In-Silico Approach
pmc-11656424.creator: Md Nasir Uddin, Md Arzo Mia, Yasmin Akter, Mohammad Al-baruni Chowdhury, Md Hadisur Rahman, Hafsa Siddiqua, Umme Salma Shathi, Abdullah Al-Mamun, Farida Siddika, Lolo Wal Marzan
pmc-11656424.description: COVID-19 caused by severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus-2 (SARS-CoV-2) had an adverse effect globally because it caused a global pandemic with several million deaths. This virus possesses spike protein that is cleaved or activated by Furin-like protease enzymes occurring by mammalian lung or respiratory cells to enter the mammalian body.

pmc-12015550.title: Oxytocin influences parental care in male threespine stickleback across multiple time scales
pmc-12015550.creator: Usan Dan, Meghan F Maciejewski, Emma Schwaiger, Alison M Bell
pmc-12015550.description: Oxytocin (OXT) and its homologs are known to regulate parental care in vertebrates, but it is unknown what role these neuropeptides may play in the evolutionary loss of care. Here, we compared two recently diverged ecotypes of threespine stickleback (Gasterosteus aculeatus) that differ in parental care.

pmc-12425782.title: High-fat diet-induced dyslipidemia drives retinal ECE-1 and ET-1 upregulation
pmc-12425782.creator: Shuo Sun, Huilan Zhang, Jing Chen, Kaiwen Hei, Yi Hou, Yanhui Yang, Chunyan Shan, Longli Zhang
pmc-12425782.description: BackgroundHigh-fat diet (HFD) consumption is a major contributor to metabolic disorders, including obesity, dyslipidemia, and endothelial dysfunction, which have systemic and ocular consequences. Emerging evidence suggests that metabolic disturbances can lead to retinal pathology, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Endothelin-1 (ET-1) and its regulatory enzyme, endothelin-converting enzyme-1 (ECE-1), play critical roles in vascular dysfunction.

pmc-12564795.title: Biomolecular Correlates of Chronic Affective Dysregulation in PTSD: CDRS and Serum Markers SUMO1, MDA, CX3CL1, and UCHL1
pmc-12564795.creator: Izabela Woźny-Rasała, Ewa Alicja Ogłodek
pmc-12564795.description: Post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD) is frequently comorbid with persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia), indicating shared neurobiological pathways that influence stress modulation, emotional regulation, and neurohormonal adaptation. This study examines the roles of serum biomarkers—small ubiquitin-like modifier 1 (SUMO1), malondialdehyde (MDA), fractalkine (CX3CL1), and ubiquitin C-terminal hydrolase L1 (UCHL1)—involved in oxidative stress management, neuroimmune regulation, and neuronal proteostasis.

pmc-12604675.title: Re‐Evaluating Access in Healthcare: Focus on Quality of Care
pmc-12604675.creator: Allen M Chen
pmc-12604675.description: The ability of patients to readily and seamlessly obtain healthcare services is a crucial element of high‐quality medical care. Access—defined by the National Academy of Medicine as “the timely use of personal health services to achieve the best health outcome”—directly impacts individual and population health as efforts to optimize access inherently promote well‐being and reduce disparities.

pmc-12971779.title: Food sources of macro- and micronutrients in young children and adults following vegan, vegetarian, and omnivorous diets
pmc-12971779.creator: Venla Tilli, Topi Hovinen, Elina Kettunen, Riitta Freese, Suvi T Itkonen, Maijaliisa Erkkola, Anu Suomalainen, Liisa Korkalo
pmc-12971779.description: PurposeUnderstanding key nutrient sources in the rapidly changing food environment is essential for advising balanced food choices across different diets. We examined the main food sources of macro- and micronutrients in Finnish children and their caregivers following vegan (VGN), vegetarian or pesco-vegetarian (VGT), and omnivorous (OMN) diets.

pmc-13564398.title: Association between youth athletes’ sports specialization and injuries: a systematic review and meta-analysis
pmc-13564398.creator: Guannan Lai, Bin-Bin Fang, Weijie Wang, Frank J.H. Lu, Wei-Jiun Shen
pmc-13564398.description: IntroductionThe purpose of this study was to conduct a systematic review and meta-analysis to examine the specialization–injury relationship, and explore whether the specialization–injury relationship is moderated by study design, sport type, age, sex, and injury measurement type, injury mechanism, and anatomical location.
